01 — The Spark

A Teacher. A Throat Condition.
Thousands of Seekers.

Acharya Prashant has dedicated his life to spiritual discourse — answering questions, dismantling illusions, and guiding people toward clarity. His platform hosts live sessions where anyone can ask anything about spirituality, philosophy, and the nature of the self.

But there's a human reality behind every live session: AP has a throat condition. Every session costs him physically. And yet, session after session, the same questions keep coming — asked by new seekers who haven't yet found the answers already given a hundred times before.

"What if the wisdom he's already shared could answer the questions he's being asked again — so the next live session could go deeper, not just repeat?"

— The design hypothesis that started this project

This wasn't a brief handed to me. I spotted the problem, felt its weight, and gave myself 48 hours to design a solution. ASK AP is that solution.

02 — The Problem

Two Sides of the
Same Friction

For Acharya Prashant

The Weight of Repetition

  • Throat condition makes every session a physical cost
  • Repetitive questions consume time meant for deeper discourse
  • No scalable way to address the same query for thousands simultaneously
  • Valuable teachings get buried under surface-level Q&A
For the Spiritual Seeker

The Wait for Clarity

  • Answers only accessible during scheduled live sessions
  • Vast library of content — but no intelligent way to search it
  • Generic spiritual advice online feels unreliable and watered-down
  • Questions arise at any time; guidance is available only sometimes

03 — Research & Insights

Scrappy, Honest,
Intentional Research

With 48 hours on the clock, this wasn't a multi-week research sprint. But it was deliberate. I drew from three honest sources:

Observational

Watching Live Sessions

I spent time watching AP's live sessions on YouTube and the app. The pattern was visible within minutes — the same categories of questions, asked by different people, session after session. Meaning, philosophy, relationships, purpose.

User Validation

A Subscriber's Perspective

A close friend who actively uses the Acharya Prashant app shared her experience firsthand. The frustration of waiting for the next live session to get an answer to a question that arose at midnight — that detail shaped the 24/7 availability as a core design requirement.

"I had a question at 11pm on a Tuesday. The next live session was four days away. I just... sat with the confusion."

— App subscriber, informal conversation
Key Insight

Credibility Is Non-Negotiable in Spiritual Guidance

Generic AI answers feel hollow in a spiritual context. Users don't just want an answer — they want to know it comes from a trusted source. This single insight drove the entire source-citation design decision: every answer must show where it came from within AP's own body of work.

05 — Design Process

48 Hours.
One Feature. Start to Finish.

I set myself a constraint: design a complete, portfolio-ready feature from insight to final screens in a single weekend. No half-measures. Here's how the time broke down.

01

Observe & Define

Watched live sessions, identified the repetition pattern, talked to a subscriber, wrote the problem statement.

→
02

Persona & Flow

Defined Kimaya as the primary user. Mapped the full user flow including edge cases — off-topic queries, no-match states, history retrieval.

→
03

Lo-fi Paper Wireframes

Pen on paper first — layout and hierarchy sketched by hand before touching Figma. Three key screens roughed out to validate the flow.

→
04

High-Fidelity UI

Built full-fidelity screens matching the app's existing design language — warm tones, clean type, the ASK AP gradient identity.

User Flow

The flow covers the full journey — from landing on ASK AP to receiving a sourced answer. It also handles edge cases: off-topic queries get a gentle redirect, no-match results offer the closest related content, and users can submit unanswered questions for the next live Q&A session.

Lo-fi Paper Wireframes
01 / 03

Pen on lined paper before any pixel was pushed. The structure was clear from the first sketch — the source tabs, the follow-up input, the suggested questions on the empty state. Paper wireframes forced the right decisions early.

06 — The Feature: ASK AP

From Question
to Clarity in Three Steps

ASK AP sits at the centre of the app's bottom navigation — visible to every user on every screen. The feature follows a single, deliberate flow.

Entry Point — From the App Feed
Design Decision

Centre Nav Placement

Placing ASK AP at the centre of the bottom navigation bar — elevated slightly above the other tabs — signals its primacy without disrupting the existing app structure. It's always one tap away, regardless of where the user is in their session.

Step 1 — Ask
01 / 03
Step 2 — Processing
Design Decision

The Gradient Ring as AI Identity

The teal-to-magenta gradient ring is ASK AP's visual signature — used consistently across the input field, loading state, and as the Answer section icon. It signals "AI is working" without mimicking generic chatbot patterns. It feels native to the spiritual aesthetic of the app.

Step 3 — Answer with Sources
01 / 03
The Source Tabs — Shorts/Videos · Reads · Quotes · Posters

Answers Matched to How You Learn

Different seekers engage with knowledge differently. Some need to hear it explained in a video. Some prefer reading. Some need a quote to sit with. The source tabs let the AI surface the same answer through different content formats — and let the user choose how they want to receive it.

Bonus — History
Design Decision

Revisit, Don't Repeat

Insights from spiritual teachings often land differently the second time. The history feature allows seekers to return to previous answers as they grow — finding new meaning in the same response they read three months ago. It turns a chat log into a personal archive of spiritual inquiry.

07 — Key Design Decisions

Four Choices That
Define the Feature

01

Source citations are mandatory, not optional

In a spiritual context, an unsourced AI answer carries zero weight. Every response in ASK AP is anchored to real content from AP's teachings — a book page, a video timestamp, a quote. This is what separates ASK AP from a generic chatbot.

02

Honest failure states over hallucinated answers

If the AI can't find a confident match, it says so clearly and offers the closest related content — plus an option to submit the question for the next live session. Honesty is a spiritual value. The UI had to reflect it.

03

Voice input as a first-class interaction

Many spiritual seekers come to the app during reflective, quiet moments — not heads-down typing sessions. Voice input with a distinctive visual state (the rainbow glow border) makes asking a question feel natural and unhurried.

04

The gradient ring as a consistent AI identity

Rather than borrowing ChatGPT or Siri visual patterns, ASK AP needed its own AI identity. The teal-purple-magenta gradient ring appears at every touchpoint — input field, loading, answer header — making the AI presence feel unified and intentional.

08 — Reflections

What I'd Do
With More Time

A 48-hour solo challenge forces prioritisation. Here's what I'd explore next if this moved into a real product sprint.

User Testing with Real Seekers

Validate the source tab design with actual AP app users. Does filtering by content type help or add friction in the moment of seeking an answer?

Multilingual Support

AP's audience spans Hindi, English, and regional languages. The feature would need voice and text input in multiple languages — and sourced answers that match the language of the question.

Admin Dashboard for AP's Team

Which questions are asked most often? Which ones return no confident match? This data could directly inform future live sessions and content creation priorities.

"The best features don't add more noise — they make the signal clearer. ASK AP exists to surface the right teaching, for the right seeker, at the right moment."

— Design principle behind ASK AP
